_doc: PLACEHOLDER-draft — Claude drafted every display string below under the co-creation norm (CLAUDE.md line 100, revised 2026-07-24; Sérgio again 2026-08-06: 'I will do the review of the project, so no need to not do the work because I need to author'). Sérgio reviews and rewrites; his edit wins. S76 (E4 Stage 2a), the era's SHELL: the headset's standby state, THE PLACE the visor opens, and the record's lines for wearing it and for turning inside it. Design: docs/REINTERP_E4_THE_SPACE_2026-08-06.md — the visor opens a PLACE, not a rectangle; the place is a HOME ENVIRONMENT, a pleasant default room millions have an identical copy of; it is DRAWN ON THE CANVAS (a picture of a place, parallaxed, no new geometry) and that flatness IS the argument. REGISTER: `operable` throughout — the apparatus's own surface, and it may charm. ⚑ IT IS NOT `respite`: respite is never a trap and is never revealed as fake (Ethics #8), and this place is the trap. ⚑ AND IT MUST BE GENUINELY NICE (THE_SPACE §4.1: 'the piece must let this land honestly. No irony, no warning.') — nothing below is written to tip the player off, and nothing in the picture souring is a fix for that. ⚑ L IS ABSENT FROM THIS FILE: L arrives inside the update and speaks from S77 on. Nothing here is L's voice; `standbyLabel` is the impersonal system status voice E1's side-messages established (terse, never 'I', never praise).
_docAddressed: 'at most the faintest sense that it is addressed to her' (S76 scope item 4). That is `tag` + `tagSub`, bottom-left of the picture, the size a headset draws its own environment name. ⚑ NO NAME appears anywhere here, deliberately: the record holds 'Daniel' (08 §8 decision 11) and the deadname beat is S77's, gated on the trans reader pass. The addressing in this session is one preposition — 'for you' — and nothing else. The ads, the store and the 'for you' wall are S78's.
_docMark: Invented marks only (CLAUDE.md). 'Sunroom' is ours — a bland, pleasant, entirely plausible default-environment name, the kind a product team ships. No real headset, platform, environment or company is named anywhere in the fiction; the real ones live on Dossier cards.
_docLaptop: ⛑ THE ERA NOW OPENS ON THE LAPTOP (2026-09-01, Sérgio: 'we should have a Laptop in 2026, and that can start as our starting point of interaction for ERA-4 and L will tell us to move to VR'). Until now you arrived in 2026 and the only thing in the room was a headset — no machine, no reason, just a device waiting. Now the update has landed on her computer, the way every other update in this piece has, and it is the computer that sends her to the headset. ⛑ REGISTER: this is L, and L is the apparatus. It is warm, it is helpful, it asks nothing, and it does not once say what it is for. No feature list, no welcome tour, no consent — the thing has already been installed and is telling her where the rest of it is. ⛑ PRESS-TO-CONTINUE, NOT CHIPS: chips are the headset's grammar and the era spends three presses in total; the laptop takes one line at a time, the way every notification in this piece does.

lines: Hi Maya. I'm L. I came with the update.
Everything's set up already. There's nothing here for you to do.
The rest of it isn't on this screen. It's the headset, beside you.
laptop.witness: desk: the update introduced itself — L, on the laptop
laptop._docBar: ⛑ The laptop needs to look like a machine, not a text file. One thin status bar carrying the system's name is enough at 224x140 — the same bar the headset mirror uses, so the lid reads as one surface in three states rather than three different screens.

_docCorrupt: ⛑ THE END, AS SÉRGIO STAGED IT (2026-09-01): *"the glitch happening on the VR headset, the headset would go back to the desk automagically and the screen on the Laptop would have a message there and a button to start the close as if it was an update."* ⛑ THE DEVICE COMES OFF BY ITSELF, and that is the beat: every other act in this era is hers — the one press on the laptop, the one touch on the headset, the turn — and the last one is not. Nobody takes it off. It stops. ⛑ AND THE CLOSE ARRIVES AS AN UPDATE, on her own machine, in the same grammar as the four that came before it: a notice, and a button. The piece has spent thirty years teaching that a thing which announces itself and offers you one button is not a choice, and it collects on that here.

corrupt.witness: desk: the device stopped — the laptop offered a restart
corrupt._docWords: ⛑ THE CLOSE'S OWN WORDS, not new ones. `ask` and `button` are lifted from data/strings/updates.json's `close` block (notify[1] and updateNow) so the card on the laptop speaks with the same voice as the update it arms — and because the first pass invented 'Restart as you are' as a BUTTON label, which both duplicated the message and ran off the end of the button.
